issues.description: Close message string is 'Close' but PR description and Deepgram docs require 'CloseStream'.
issues.detail: _CLOSE_MSG sends {"type": "Close"} while the PR text and linked Deepgram Speak/Listen spec specify {"type": "CloseStream"}. If the server ignores the unknown type, the fix is a no-op and the original bug remains. Reconcile the wire literal against Deepgram's actual contract before merge.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout is not a drain handshake.
issues.detail: The stated postcondition is that remaining audio/transcripts are flushed before close, but one receive() consumes at most one frame, which may be a stray audio chunk or ping rather than a terminal ack. Either loop until a Close/CloseResponse (bounded by an overall deadline) or document this as best-effort grace, not a drain.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` around send/receive swallows real bugs.
issues.detail: Wrapping the close sequence in except Exception conflates expected ConnectionResetError/WebSocketError with programming faults and cancellation-adjacent errors, all surfacing as a single warning. Narrow to ConnectionError/aiohttp websocket errors (mirror the STT path) so logs carry real information and genuine bugs are not hidden.

issues.description: Control-message constants should be shared/centralized rather than duplicated per class.
issues.detail: STT already encodes the same Deepgram control vocabulary; defining _FLUSH_MSG/_CLOSE_MSG as TTS class attributes creates two copies of one protocol fact that will drift. Move them to a module-level (or shared protocol module) constant so STT and TTS reference one source of truth.

issues.description: Flush-before-Close is an unjustified second behavior change bundled into the fix.
issues.detail: The PR title and docs reference only CloseStream, yet the diff unconditionally sends a Flush first. Either state why Flush is required in addition to Close (with a precondition/postcondition argument) or drop it. Behavior changes should not ride along inside a bugfix patch without justification.

issues.description: 1.0s close-wait is an unmeasured, undocumented magic number.
issues.detail: The PR claims this prevents lingering-session 429s, but 1.0s has no cited measurement or rationale and could be too short under jitter or too long on hot paths. Name the constant, cite the measurement that produced it, or expose it as configurable.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the fix moves in the right direction — sending an explicit control message before WebSocket teardown — but is not yet correct. The load-bearing defect is that the code sends {"type": "Close"} while the PR description and Deepgram docs specify {"type": "CloseStream"}; if the server ignores the unknown type the patch is a no-op. Secondary structural issues: a single receive() does not actually drain remaining audio, the bare except Exception hides real bugs, and the protocol constants should be shared with STT rather than duplicated. Reconcile the wire literal, turn the wait into a bounded drain loop (or document it as best-effort), and narrow the exception handler before merge.
